newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs pare losses, but end down on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs pare losses, but end down on weak cash.

text.p: Continued weakness in cash pork products and expectations for further losses in cash hogs kept pressure on CME hog futures at the close despite late shortcovering, traders said.
Hogs closed off 0.975 cent to up 0.050 cent, with April off most at 72.425 cents a lb. Only thinly traded distant June and July were up and posted new contract highs.
Pork bellies ended mostly up 0.850 to off 0.200, with May up 0.825 at 79.800 cents.
Weakness in cash pork products and lower live indications for Wednesday influenced trade late after early influence from Taiwan and Japan stories, they said.
"There's general disappointment that the wholesale pork market hasn't responded to all the talk about exports," said Dale Durchholz, AgriVisor Services Inc market analyst.
Durchholz added that "as long as Japan's not on that (Taiwan) list it's not going to make a lot of difference" to expected U.S. pork exports.
Reports that Taiwan may have as many as 13 countries that would take pork certifited as unaffected by the foot-and-mouth outbreak weighed heavily on hog futures early.
But analysts did note that Japan meat sales have slowed due to e-coli and other meat concerns.

Durchholz said not only e-coli, but the foot-and-mouth outbreak in Taiwan and "Mad Cow" in Britain have made for a general lack of confidence among Japanese consumers and meat sales have declined in that country.

Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien bought June late after selling early. Lind-Waldock and Rosenthal Collins were late sellers. In hog options, Iowa Grain actively spread the June/August 82 call spread, pit sources said.
Pork bellies ran up again late after mixed trade early with expectations of a bullish out-of-town report and expected bottoming in cash lending support, traders said.

The weekly out-of-town storage report was expected to show only a small in-movement last week and cash bellies were expected to bottom in the $70 to $72 per cwt where they are currently trading, they said.
After the close, CME reported a net in-movement of 255,000 lbs. This compares with early analyst estimates on the report of in 250,000 to 500,000 lbs and later estimates of in 200,000 to 600,000 lbs.
Refco and Rosenthal bought May late with locals also covering short positions, pit sources said.
